study type: secondary analysis of cross-sectional survey data
exposure: birth setting (midwife-led birth unit, home births with health professionals, home births without health professionals, hospital)
cohort: The study included self-reported data from 45,953 women aged 15-49 years who participated in the 2007, 2012, and 2017 Indonesian Demographic Health Surveys.
finding: Pregnancy risk and barriers to health care access are key elements associated with neonatal mortality, with midwifery-led birth units being an accessible option with low odds of first-day neonatal mortality in Indonesia.
mod_finding: Home births, both with and without health professionals present, were associated with higher first-day neonatal mortality compared to births in midwife-led birth units.
